clue.text: A piece of poetry seen in most Anzac campaigns

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase is visible inside it, sitting across the word boundaries

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A poem that turns up in the stories of nearly every Anzac military campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The Anzacs were the Australian and New Zealand Army Corps of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a verse, one grouped section of lines within a poem.

clue.text: Five in twisted lariat show pangs of birth

indicators.note: the numeral is placed in the middle of the other letters
twisting something bends it out of its original order

explanation.surface: A rope trick going wrong as a cowboy's lasso snarls.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is an old word for the pain and effort of childbirth, labour.

clue.text: Famous for having no dining furniture

parts.note: the piece of furniture one eats at

explanation.surface: A household renowned for owning no table to eat at.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'no table' and the clue explains itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone notable is well known and worth noting, so famous.

clue.text: Eastern leader about to conclude the list of events

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: an Aga is a commander or chief in Ottoman Turkey

explanation.surface: An Oriental ruler about to wrap up the programme of a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA opens to hold END: AG-END-A.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the schedule of items to be dealt with, often for a meeting.

clue.text: Very unfriendly when its back in a hole

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the word reads from its end
the turned word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written, split around the other piece

explanation.surface: An animal turns surly when its back is down a burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile means openly antagonistic, the opposite of friendly.

clue.text: Talks about the French holiday cottages

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps the other

explanation.surface: Discussions about the French and their holiday homes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chalets are wooden houses typical of Alpine resorts, often rented for holidays.

clue.text: See us in casual surroundings — no change when 100 leave

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so this letter is taken out of the built word
the word casual forms the surroundings, so the other piece sits within it

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: An invitation to meet in a relaxed setting, with a note that nothing alters when a hundred people depart.
explanation.walkthrough: US placed in CASUAL gives CASUSUAL; 'leave' removes C (100) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying things go on as usual means the routine continues without any alteration.

clue.text: Kind of goal she's after in protective footwear

indicators.note: a kind of something is a version of it, so these letters appear in a different form

explanation.surface: A sports report about a woman's goal scored while wearing boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the second piece behind the rearranged first one.
explanation.definitionFit: Galoshes are rubber overshoes worn to keep ordinary shoes dry in wet weather.

clue.text: Cloak for the male taking in the Northern Territory

indicators.note: to take something in is to admit it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: taken as written; 'the' just reads naturally
the standard abbreviation of the Australian territory

explanation.surface: Asking what garment a man should wear on a trip to the Northern Territory.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the postal abbreviation for Australia's Northern Territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantle is a loose sleeveless cloak, an old word for an outer wrap.

clue.text: Clue's not for disturbing bats

indicators.note: disturbing things throws them out of their settled order

parts.note: every letter of these two words, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A hint that is not meant to upset a batsman, or the bats themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like a verb or a cricket term, but it is the plural noun for the flying mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: The noctule is a large European species of insect-eating bat.

clue.text: Dressed in what you find in red bag

indicators.note: the setter loosely asks what can be made from the letters, a weak signal for rearranging them

parts.note: every letter of these two words

explanation.surface: Clothes are found by rummaging in a red bag.
explanation.walkthrough: The indicator is unusually vague; the six letters of the last two words simply rearrange to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be garbed is to be clothed, garb being a word for distinctive clothing.

clue.text: Dye for articles English and Italian?

explanation.surface: A question about what dye suits English and Italian goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' is grammatical: one article from each language joins up.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it, a crossword stalwart.

clue.text: The Spanish and German church official

explanation.surface: A churchman who is Spanish and German by heritage.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a lay office-holder in Presbyterian and other churches.

clue.text: Scholarly way to ride ute

indicators.note: a way to make something is a method of forming it, signalling the letters are reworked

parts.note: every letter of these two words

explanation.surface: An academic's way of travelling in a pickup truck.
explanation.walkthrough: A ute is the Australian name for a utility vehicle, a small pickup truck.
explanation.definitionFit: An erudite person has deep learning, so the word means scholarly.

clue.text: Sirius returns as rodents' deity

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the phrase is read backwards

explanation.surface: A star comes back as the god worshipped by rats.
explanation.definitionFit: Sirius, the brightest star in the night sky, is popularly called the Dog Star.

clue.text: Again encloses prewar school head, in a way

indicators.note: treated in some way means the letters are reshaped into another order
'head' keeps only the first letter of 'school'

explanation.surface: A headmaster again shelters a school from before the war.
explanation.definitionFit: To rewrap something is to enclose it in wrapping once more.

clue.text: Upset lease to support one's painting

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A disrupted rental agreement that is meant to fund an artist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a thing whose purpose is to hold up a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand that holds an artist's canvas upright while working.

clue.text: Its aura is haphazard in European country

indicators.note: a haphazard arrangement has no set order

parts.note: every letter of these two words

explanation.surface: A country whose charm or atmosphere is random.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a landlocked nation of central Europe, capital Vienna.

clue.text: Doreen's arranged to sign the cheque in support

indicators.note: arranged letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A woman makes arrangements to put her name on a cheque as backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To endorse a cheque is to sign its back; to endorse a cause is to back it.

clue.text: Jane Austen's female comes back in the morning to me

indicators.note: coming back is travelling the opposite way, so the letters are read from the end

explanation.surface: A woman from a novel returns to the speaker in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Austen's novel Emma.

clue.text: Study in art can become passionate

indicators.note: one word sits in the other, inside its letters

parts.note: taken as written, split around the other piece
a den or study is a private workroom

explanation.surface: Learning art can make a person fervent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning with enthusiasm or feeling, fervent.

clue.text: Dwell in some house whose chores I delight in

indicators.note: found in some of the following words, that is within part of them

parts.note: letters running across these three words

explanation.surface: A happy homemaker who enjoys every household task.
explanation.walkthrough: The concealed run starts partway through 'chores', after two words of scene-setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live somewhere as one's home, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Left all alone, causing disturbed rest, indeed

indicators.note: causing here hints that the rest goes into the action, so its letters are put inside the other word

parts.note: read as 'in deed', the word gives deed, an action

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of rest are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lonely person whose sleep is broken, and who is truly abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'indeed' as 'in deed': the action named supplies the outer letters, with the jumbled rest set inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abandoned is to be left on one's own by everyone, a sense of the past participle of forsake.

clue.text: John Kerr or some others hide their mistakes

indicators.note: the words conceal something within them

parts.note: letters straddling Kerr, or and some

explanation.surface: A dig at Governor-General John Kerr and others for covering up blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Kerr was the Australian Governor-General who dismissed the Whitlam government in 1975.
explanation.definitionFit: Errors are mistakes, the plain synonym in plural form.

clue.text: A pot's one kind of mis printed recipe measure

indicators.note: something misprinted has its type set wrongly, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, joining the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook complains that the quantity in a recipe has been printed wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is both part of the letters to rearrange and the start of 'one kind of'; the paper prints 'mis printed' as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaspoon is a standard small unit of volume used in cooking instructions.

clue.text: Not to be sick in 2 but take the Spanish and move about

indicators.note: 'not' removes the sense that follows from the word it applies to

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell
EL is the Spanish article, added on

explanation.surface: Advice not to get ill while in labour pains, but to get up and walk around.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 2 is TRAVAIL; dropping AIL leaves TRAV, then EL completes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel is to go from place to place, to journey about.
